date_note: FinCEN's statement was issued on Tuesday per Türkiye Gazetesi's article of 25 November; resolved to 24 November.
geo_basis: agency headquarters, Washington DC (US Treasury unit)
title: FinCEN says an unauthorized party gained access to a limited subset of its systems
summary: CyberScoop reports FinCEN, a US Treasury unit, said an unauthorized party gained access to a limited subset of its systems and that it took some systems offline as a precaution. GovInfoSecurity says FinCEN states the scope and impact are still under investigation. Cyber Security News says a FinCEN official told Reuters no breach of the Bank Secrecy Act or beneficial ownership databases has been found so far.
plain: FinCEN, a US Treasury unit, says an unauthorized party got into a limited subset of its systems. It took some systems offline as a precaution. A FinCEN official told Reuters, as relayed by Cyber Security News, that no breach of two databases has been found so far.
exec: FinCEN says some services may be temporarily unavailable and it is extending deadlines for affected filers.
action: No action needed; for awareness. FinCEN says it is extending deadlines for filers affected by the disruption.

sources.name: Türkiye Gazetesi: ABD'nin kritik kurumlarına peş peşe siber saldırı!

validation.note: CyberScoop (relaying FinCEN's notice) and Türkiye Gazetesi are independent publishers stating the core fact; AITNews relays The Verge. FinCEN's own notice was not read. DataBreaches.net returned 403 and Punto Informatico reset the connection.
